newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi auditor resigns in auto tag scandal.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi auditor resigns in auto tag scandal.

text.p: Mississippi state Auditor Steve Patterson said Thursday he would resign from office, and has agreed to plead guilty to a misdemeanor charge of filing false statements.

Patterson was accused last year of trying to avoid paying past due license fees on his personal vehicle, a Range Rover. In February, 1995, he submitted a statement saying the vehicle had been in a repair shop for 18 months and had not been used on Mississippi streets since his license tag expired on Oct 31, 1993.
The repair company president whose name appeared on the letter has denied signing it, and said the vehicle was never in his shop.
Attorney General Mike Moore said previously he would take the case to a grand jury this week and seek an indictment.

Patterson has agreed to enter a guilty plea by Oct 18, which would eliminate the need for an indictment. He released a statement saying he would submit his resignation to Gov. Kirk Fordice later this week.
"Much controversy has plagued me, my family and my administration concerning my car tags. Today I am hopefully putting an end to this controversy," Patterson said in the statement.
Under Mississippi law, the governor will appoint a replacement to serve the remaining 3.5 years of Patterson's term.
